theory.intro: A **continuous random variable** can take any value in an interval. For a continuous distribution, the probability of any one exact value is $0$, because a single point has zero width and hence zero area under the density curve.
facts: A continuous random variable comes from measuring something such as a length, time, mass, temperature or speed.
Its possible values fill an interval such as $0 < x < 100$, so they cannot be listed one by one.

An underlying measurement can be continuous while its rounded recorded value is discrete. For example, true mass varies continuously, but mass recorded to the nearest gram takes separate whole-number values.
$P(X = a) = 0$ for every single value $a$, since one point has no width on the number line.
Individual values have probability $0$. An interval can have positive probability, written $P(a < X < b)$.
Because the endpoints contribute nothing, $P(a < X < b) = P(a \le X \le b) = P(a \le X < b) = P(a < X \le b)$.
For the same reason $P(X < c) = P(X \le c)$ and $P(X > c) = P(X \ge c)$.
The complement rule still holds, so $P(X > c) = 1 - P(X \le c)$.

workedExamples.question_text: At a delivery depot, let $T$ be the true time taken to unload a van and $N$ be the number of parcels in the van. State whether each random variable is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$T$ is continuous because time is measured and can take any value in an interval.

$N$ is discrete because parcels are counted; the possible values are separate whole numbers.

workedExamples.question_text: A shop sells belts in sizes $7$, $7.5$, $8$, $8.5$ and $9$. Let $S$ be the size purchased and $L$ be the customer's true waist measurement. State whether each random variable is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$S$ is discrete because the available sizes are separate listed values. Discrete values need not be whole numbers.

$L$ is continuous because true waist measurement can take any value in an interval.

workedExamples.question_text: For a randomly selected delivery, let $M$ be the true mass of a parcel, $R$ its mass recorded to the nearest $0.2$ kg, and $N$ the number of parcels delivered to the address. State whether each random variable is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$M$ is continuous because true mass can take any value in an interval.

$R$ is discrete because the recorded masses occur in separate steps of $0.2$ kg. Rounding changes the record, not the true mass.

$N$ is discrete because parcels are counted in whole numbers.

foundation.question_text: Let $T$ be the time, in seconds, a swimmer takes to complete $100$ m. State whether $T$ is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
Time is measured, not counted.
Any value in an interval such as $50 < t < 70$ is possible.
$T$ is continuous.

foundation.question_text:
Let $N$ be the number of text messages a person sends in a day.
State whether $N$ is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
Messages are counted, not measured.
The possible values are the separate steps $0, 1, 2, \dots$
$N$ is discrete.

foundation.question_text:
The mass of a bag of flour is recorded to the nearest gram.
Let $M$ be the true mass before rounding.
State whether $M$ is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
Mass is measured, so the true mass can be any value in an interval.
Recording it to the nearest gram rounds the record, not the quantity.
$M$ is continuous.

foundation.question_text:
A quiz has $20$ questions, each worth one mark for a correct answer and zero otherwise. Let $S$ be the mark scored.
State whether $S$ is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
foundation.solution_text:
The mark is a count of correct answers.
The possible values are the whole numbers from $0$ to $20$.
$S$ is discrete.

development.question_text:
A sensor measures a car's true speed $U$, in kilometres per hour, and records its speed $R$ to the nearest whole kilometre per hour.
State whether each random variable is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
development.solution_text:
$U$ is continuous because true speed can take any value in an interval.
$R$ is discrete because the rounded record takes separate whole-number values.

development.question_text:
A shop stocks shoe sizes $5$, $5.5$, $6$, $6.5$, $7$, $7.5$ and $8$. Let $S$ be the size bought by a randomly chosen customer and $L$ be that customer's true foot length, in centimetres.
State whether each random variable is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
development.solution_text:
$S$ is discrete because the stocked sizes form a listed set of separate values, even though some are not whole numbers.
$L$ is continuous because true foot length can take any value in an interval.

development.question_text:
A machine records the volume of milk in a carton, correct to two decimal places. Let $V$ be the true volume, in litres, before rounding.
State whether $V$ is discrete or continuous, and justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
Volume is measured, so the true volume can be any value in an interval.
The rounded record is discrete, but $V$ denotes the true volume.
$V$ is continuous.

mastery.question_text:
For a randomly chosen batch of $48$ containers, let $N$ be the number with a defect, $M$ the true mass of a randomly chosen container, and $R$ its mass recorded to the nearest $0.5$ gram.
State whether each random variable is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
mastery.solution_text:
$N$ is discrete because it takes whole-number values from $0$ to $48$.
$M$ is continuous because true mass can take any value in an interval.
$R$ is discrete because recorded masses occur in separate steps of $0.5$ gram.

mastery.question_text:
A randomly chosen swimmer completes a $200$ m race. Let $T$ be the true finishing time in seconds, $R$ the time recorded to the nearest $0.01$ second, and $N$ the number of swimmers who finish before this swimmer.
State whether each random variable is discrete or continuous, and give a reason.
mastery.solution_text:
$T$ is continuous because true finishing time can take any value in an interval.
$R$ is discrete because recorded times occur in separate steps of $0.01$ second.
$N$ is discrete because swimmers are counted in whole numbers.
